title: Passive form (〜られる / 〜れる)
meaning: "be done (by someone)". Also the "suffering passive" (迷惑の受身) where the subject is adversely affected.
simpleExplanation: The passive says something was done TO the subject: ほめる (praise) → ほめられる (be praised). The person who does the action is marked with に. Japanese also has a "suffering passive": 雨に降られた ("I got rained on") shows the speaker was affected, usually badly. If someone steps on your foot, you say 足を踏まれた, keeping を on the foot and making yourself the subject.
whenUsed: Three main jobs: (1) plain passive, when the receiver matters more than the doer (この本は多くの人に読まれている); (2) suffering passive, to complain about what someone did to you (財布を盗まれた, 友達に来られて勉強できなかった); (3) neutral facts about creations and discoveries with によって (この寺は8世紀に建てられた). Also used as a light honorific (lesson 71).
formation: Group 1: ない-stem + れる: 書く→書かれる, 読む→読まれる, 踏む→踏まれる, 言う→言われる
Group 2: ない-stem + られる: 食べる→食べられる, ほめる→ほめられる
Group 3: する→される, 来る→来られる (こられる)
Doer + に (先生にほめられた); for authors/builders: によって
Conjugates as Group 2: 言われます / 言われない / 言われた

diagram.root: 書く / 食べる / する / 来る

branches.label: Group 2: be eaten (same shape as potential)

examples.ja: 私は先生にほめられました。
examples.reading: わたしは せんせいに ほめられました。
examples.en: I was praised by the teacher.
examples.note: Plain passive: doer 先生 takes に.

examples.ja: この本は多くの人に読まれています。
examples.reading: この ほんは おおくの ひとに よまれています。
examples.en: This book is read by many people.
examples.note: Passive for general statements about a thing; the doer is a vague group.

examples.reading: でんしゃで あしを ふまれた。
examples.en: I got my foot stepped on in the train.
examples.note: Suffering passive: the foot keeps を, the speaker is the affected subject.

examples.ja: 電車の中で財布を盗まれてしまった。
examples.reading: でんしゃのなかで さいふを ぬすまれてしまった。
examples.en: I had my wallet stolen on the train.
examples.note: Suffering passive with を: the speaker is the victim, the wallet is the object.

examples.ja: この橋は百年前に作られました。
examples.reading: このはしは ひゃくねんまえに つくられました。
examples.en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.
examples.note: Neutral passive for things that were made; if you name the builder, use によって.

similarGrammar.difference: Group 2 potential and passive look the same (食べられる). Potential sentences have が on the object and no doer; passive sentences have a doer with に.
The same form used about a respected person (先生が来られた = the teacher came). No に-doer and the subject is someone you respect.
"Was made to do": the subject was forced to act. Plain passive: the subject had something done to them.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は友達がケーキを食べられた。
commonMistakes.right: 私は友達にケーキを食べられた。
commonMistakes.why: In the passive the doer takes に, not が. "My friend ate my cake (and I was upset)."

commonMistakes.wrong: 私の足は電車で踏まれた。
commonMistakes.right: 私は電車で足を踏まれた。
commonMistakes.why: Japanese prefers to make the affected person the subject and keep を on the body part or possession.

commonMistakes.wrong: この小説は夏目漱石に書かれた。
commonMistakes.right: この小説は夏目漱石によって書かれた。
commonMistakes.why: For creators of works (write, build, paint, discover), use によって instead of に.

usageNotes: The suffering passive can use intransitive verbs, which English cannot: 雨に降られる, 友達に来られる, 父に死なれる. The nuance is "and it was a problem for me".
Japanese uses the passive less than English for neutral facts. In daily conversation, prefer the active with a clear doer when there is no emotional nuance.
Feelings and commonly used passives: 言われる (be told), 呼ばれる (be called), 誘われる (be invited), 叱られる (be scolded), 頼まれる (be asked).
jlptTips: Passive questions almost always contain a に-marked doer or a victim + を. If you see 〜に…を and a verb blank, think suffering passive (〜に財布を取られた).
Options typically include the causative (〜せる) and potential of the same verb. Confirm the subject is receiving the action before choosing 〜れる / 〜られる.
